claims.statement: The Organizer window is a three-column layout — outline tree, row list, details — with two tabs ("Wissen" annotations, "Titel" works), built entirely in code via ztoolkit.Dialog and the DOM builders in organizerDom.ts, which is why its UI strings live in organizer/strings.ts with German and English copies instead of Fluent files.

OrganizerFactory.open() enforces one window per Zotero process: if getOpenWindow() finds a live window containing #flexannotate-root (cache first, then Services.wm enumeration), it un-minimizes and focuses it, and when a collectionID is requested it re-scopes that window via its per-window Ctx from the windowCtx WeakMap instead of opening a duplicate; the Ctx is stored in a WeakMap keyed by Window rather than a module flag because the plugin scope is global while windows are not.

Four entry points open the Organizer, all funneling into OrganizerFactory.open(): a toolbar button inserted into #zotero-tabs-toolbar before the sync button (end of the toolbar if the sync button is absent), the Tools menubar via Zotero.MenuManager (registerPluginMenu, key zotero-tools-flexannotate-organizer), a Zotero 7.x DOM fallback in #menu_ToolsPopup added only when MenuManager.registerMenu is missing (label set via the attribute because Fluent sets textContent, which a XUL menuitem does not display), and a collection context-menu entry in #zotero-collectionmenu hidden on popupshowing unless a collection is selected.

OrganizerFactory.mount() wires per-window state once: it applies the theme, initializes Zotero.Styles (locator labels need the CSL locales), derives defaultScope from the main window's current library/collection, builds the initial State, stores the Ctx in the windowCtx WeakMap, and registers document-level keydown and capture-phase mousedown listeners that track the focused column, close data-menu drop-downs and end an open inline rename when the mouse is pressed outside the rename field — surviving full re-renders because they live on the document, not on panel nodes.

The window state is one State record in organizerState.ts (libraryID, noteID, roots, collectionKey, tab, allRows/rows, scope/scopeWorks, selection, node filter, query, showWorks/showCommentsInRows, saveChain, saveLog, orphans and transient UI state); panels receive a Ctx exposing doc, root, s and exactly two actions — render and the factory's replaceable confirm — and rendering is a full rebuild (renderAll) that prunes the selection to visible ids and restores each column's scroll position from a data-scroll snapshot taken before the wipe.

Column 2 renders from in-memory rows, not Zotero calls: Wissen rows come from loadAnnotationRows over the AnnotationIndex (with resolved locator type via locatorOf and readOnly from !item.isEditable()), Titel rows from Zotero.Items.getAll top-level regular items sorted by title; applyScope restricts rows to the scope's works (annotation included when its work is), and visibleRows applies the tree selection (all / none via unassignedItems / a heading via itemsUnder with subheadings) plus a keyword filter; the sections option regroups rows with groupByOutline in outline order.

Filing a row under a heading is adding the heading's §-prefixed Zotero tag: assign/unassign call fileMany/unfileMany, which wrap the batch in one Zotero.DB.executeTransaction, skip read-only items and items already carrying the tag, and return the actually-changed ids so cached rows are patched in place and a toast reports skipped rows; rows reach a heading by drag-and-drop (selection serialized as JSON under the custom MIME type text/x-flexannotate-ids onto the tree node) or via the permanent assign bar with pure multi-selection logic (applyClick/selectAll/prune); heading titles must be unique across the tree because same-named headings would share one tag.

The outline tree persists as one standalone note tagged ★outline whose payload is the JSON { v: 1, roots } after the LATTICE-OUTLINE-V1 sentinel in a 
 block (plus a presentation-only readable list); parseOutline reads only the JSON, accepts both  and
closings (Zotero rewrites them) and sanitizes malformed payloads; a collection tree lives on a second note tied by the extra tag #flexannotate-outline- — the collection key, not the id, because the key survives sync; when several notes carry ★outline, findNote/pickNewest take the newest dateModified with ties broken by the higher id.

Every outline mutation and every scope switch runs through persist()/loadScope(), which append to State.saveChain: saves execute one after another and each reads State.roots when it actually runs, so two quick edits (e.g. a rename followed by a move) can never overwrite each other with an older tree; scope switches inside the chain mean open saves still land in the old tree and two quick switches cannot create two notes; each step is logged into State.saveLog (capped at 30), failures are logged without breaking the chain, and OutlineModel.save returns the note id that is stored back on the state.
OutlineModel.save creates a new outline note with saveTx({ skipSelect: true }) so Zotero's note editor cannot open it and later write a stale copy over organizer saves.

OutlineModel.save and load run syncAnchorTags: every heading in the tree gets its §-tag anchored on the outline note itself (anchorTagDiff computes the add/remove sets, the write is skipped when there is no diff), so Zotero's tag autocomplete suggests every heading of the tree when typing § in the reader even with nothing filed; load also runs syncNoteHeading, rewriting only the first <h1> to '📚 FlexAnnotate — <label> — <scope name>' when it differs so several outline notes are distinguishable in the item list; the note itself never counts as a filed item because isOutlineNote excludes ★outline notes from gather and buildCountMap.

The organizer can be scoped to a collection: loadScope maps the chosen collection to its topmost ancestor (topmostCollection, circular-chain safe) so a subcollection shows the main collection's tree with only its own entries; on the first open of a collection without an own outline note it asks once (the replaceable confirm) whether to clone the library tree as a starting point and creates the note immediately; the tag scope of tree-spanning operations (renameTag, purgeTag, gather, counting) is the work ids of the tree's topmost collection including subcollections (treeWorkIDs), null for the library tree, which is unrestricted — so a rename in one tree cannot drag a same-named heading in another tree, while a work in two top collections deliberately shares its § tags, signalled by the 'also in tree' chip hint.

After every reload and loadScope, refreshOrphans reconciles orphaned heading tags — §-tags in the tree's scope with no matching heading, e.g. after a rename on a machine without the plugin: it builds the tag count map over the tree scope, diffs against the tree with orphanHeadingTags, stores {tag,count} in State.orphans, bails if the tree was switched mid-flight, closes a stale overlay when the result is empty, and re-renders only when something changed and the window is still open; the orphanOverlay lists tags only, each assignable to a heading via scoped OutlineModel.renameTag or removable via scoped purgeTag after a confirm showing the affected item count.

AnnotationIndex lifts all annotations of a library into a single in-memory Map of AnnRecords: build() uses Zotero.Items.getAll with asIDs and hydrates in one getAsync batch, ensureBuilt rebuilds only when the index is missing or was built for another library (builtLibraryID); a Notifier observer on item events, registered once by the annotationIndex feature at startup, patches incrementally (delete/trash drop ids, add/modify re-hydrate non-deleted annotations of the built library and drop everything else) with fire-and-forget notifications; unload unregisters the observer and clears the map.

OutlineModel.itemsWithTag, gather and buildCountMap merge AnnotationIndex hits into Zotero tag searches because Zotero omits annotations from search results — otherwise renames, heading deletion, counting and the note export would silently miss filed quotes.

The details column shows the selected row's quote, comment, source line (citationFor honours the Quick Copy style with an author/year/title fallback, placeOf formats the localized locator label plus page label), category chips with numbering/tagIndex mapping and the optional 'also in tree' hint, and open/copy/edit actions; the edit form changes exactly one annotation (quote text only for highlight/underline types, comment, page label, locator type via locatorTagChanges into the #flexannotate-locator-* tag scheme) and refuses read-only rows; openTarget deep links jump to annotations via Zotero.Reader.open(attachmentID, {annotationID: key}) — reusing an open reader tab — and to works via ZoteroPane.selectItem, bringing the main window to the front because the organizer is a separate window.

The outline footer exports in two shapes: 'Notiz' gathers everything filed under every heading (gatherAll walks the tree in outline order, items scoped to the tree's works) into a standalone Zotero note via the pure outlineToHtml/outlineToMarkdown builders (annotations as blockquotes with citation, page and zotero://open-pdf deep links), then selects it in the main window; the document buttons import a .docx/.odt outline as an append-merge (nothing deleted or moved) and export the tree as Word/ODT with heading styles and multilevel numbering, with the parsing/writing rules pure in logic/docOutline.ts and logic/docExport.ts and the Zotero-facing file pickers and ZIP I/O in doc/.

The citation dialog gets an injected outline view (not a patch): the outlineView injector adds a 'Nach Gliederung anordnen' toggle to the annotations sidebar (moved into the settings menu below 750 px, following dialog-type with a MutationObserver); when enabled an injected stylesheet hides Zotero's native columns and three containers show headings with counts, the chosen heading's items, and a preview; the view supports both annotations (grouped via buildDialogSections, merging work heading tags when enabled) and works/items (grouped via buildWorkDialogSections), switching list layouts to library mode via IOManager.toggleDialogMode; a collection picker remembers the last choice in the dialogOutlineCollection preference and falls back to the whole library when the collection is gone; Zotero's search bar is mirrored one-way into the outline list via handle-input; insertion invokes IOManager.addItemsToCitation for works or triggers Zotero's native '+' handler via a hidden annotation-row for annotations; the green 'already cited' check comes from citedWorksOf and the citedAnnotations store hooked into io.accept, and restoreLayout removes all injected elements when the view turns off.

externalApi installs Zotero.FlexAnnotate on the shared Zotero namespace at startup and removes it at shutdown, both idempotent and never clobbering an install owned by a different plugin (the conflict is logged); consumers get apiVersion, pluginID, getOutline (raw tree) and getHeadings (flat heading list with derived decimal numbers, breadcrumb path and backing tag built by logic/flatHeadings.ts, so numbers match what the organizer displays); API methods log failures and degrade to empty results instead of throwing untyped errors.

The Organizer descends from Lattice (birugit, zotero-grounded-qa), forked at v4.1.0 (commit 8d75041) under AGPL-3.0-or-later, which FlexAnnotate keeps unchanged; from Lattice it inherited the knowledge-organizer concept (§-prefixed heading tags, ★outline note with the LATTICE-OUTLINE-V1 sentinel), the annotation index and export helpers; it removed Lattice's AI components and the ideas layer (★idea notes) and added the three-column window, works+annotations filing, the works display setting, the citation-dialog outline view and collection trees with orphan reconciliation; derived files carry the 'Derived from Lattice' header and the persisted format stays Lattice-compatible.

Group-library annotations of other users are handled as read-only end to end: rows load readOnly from !item.isEditable(), render with reduced opacity, are filtered out of drag payloads, and are skipped by fileMany/unfileMany and saveAnnotation.

Organizer tests split along the repo's seam: Node unit tests (test-unit/outline.test.ts, dialogView.test.ts, selection.test.ts, scope.test.ts) pin the pure logic — computed numbering, tree operations, title uniqueness, the LATTICE-OUTLINE-V1 round-trip, dialog grouping and collection helpers — while Zotero integration tests (organizer.test.ts, toolbarButton.test.ts, toolsMenu.test.ts and the organizer sections of features.test.ts) drive the window, filing, single-window enforcement, scoped renames, orphans, the edit form, exports and anchor-tag backfills exclusively through addon.api.

docImport and docOutline provide an append-merge outline import from Word (.docx) and LibreOffice (.odt) documents: parseDocxHeadings and parseOdtHeadings extract headings via a custom XML scanner (skipping deletions and footnotes), normalizeHeadings resolves gaps and detects/strips manual numbering patterns, planOutlineImport reuses nodes under matching parents, disambiguates collisions with suffixes, and cascades tag renames via OutlineModel.renameTag, verified through an interactive preview modal before persisting.

docExport and doc/logic/docExport.ts export the outline tree to Word (.docx) and LibreOffice (.odt) files with Heading 1-9 styles and synchronized multilevel decimal numbering: buildDocxParts creates complete OOXML package parts bound to standard styles while buildOdtParts packages OpenDocument XML with uncompressed mimetype entry first, written via nsIZipWriter and launched via Zotero.launchFile.

persistentDialogPatch transforms Zotero's citation dialog into a persistent companion browsing window for Word and LibreOffice: when enabled, after citation insertion the dialog reopens at the same geometry with a synthetic CitationEditInterface io, and subsequent inserts from the browsing window queue pendingInsert and re-execute addAnnotation, where patched displayDialog intercepts the command to inject the selection into the real io without opening a redundant window, while unneeded progress bars are suppressed.

dialogPersistent and logic/persistentRect.ts manage citation dialog window bounds: relaxDialogMinWidth lowers libraryLayout.MIN_WIDTH from 1000 px to 360 px and injects CSS resetting min-width to 0 for narrow side-by-side placement; pinRect locks window geometry for 5000 ms to override Zotero's post-open resize animations before releasing for user adjustments; and bounds are debounced into persistentWindowRect, validated against screen bounds, clamped if moved to a smaller monitor, and synchronized to integration.citationDialog.windowParams.

dialogPersistent enforces inner window dimensions and handles narrow layouts (<750px) for the companion window: openWindow features set inner dimensions whereas resizeTo targets outer bounds including window chrome computed via chromeOf; pinRect intercepts win.resizeTo and win.moveTo to preserve target inner geometry and coordinates through Zotero's loading and resize phases before releasing manual control; and when narrow (<750px), responsive rules stack panels vertically and migration moves toggles into the settings menu popup.
